title: Google DeepMind’s London AI drug spinout eyes $50bn valuation
key_facts: Isomorphic Labs, a London AI drug discovery firm spun out of Google DeepMind, is reportedly in early talks to raise money at a valuation of at least $40bn, possibly up to $50bn, according to Bloomberg.
No agreement has been reached; the earlier valuation was roughly $17.5bn.
It raised $2.1bn in a Series B in May and $600m in March 2025, about $2.7bn disclosed in total.
It uses AI, building on AlphaFold, to design potential medicines for cancer and immune disorders and works with Eli Lilly, Novartis and Johnson and Johnson.
It has not yet tested its own drug candidates in humans and targets its first clinical trials by the end of 2026.
Alphabet is majority owner; Demis Hassabis is chief executive.
On Wednesday it joined Google DeepMind and Meta in a combined $300m commitment to AI models of how human cells behave, part of a $1.8bn virtual-cell effort led by Biohub.
quote_evidence: The figure could climb as high as $50bn, although negotiations remain early and no agreement has been reached.
However, despite attracting billions in investment, Isomorphic has yet to test its own drug candidates in humans.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows investor appetite for AI-designed medicines before any has reached patients.
notes: Single-source report of talks (Bloomberg via City AM); original Bloomberg page not opened.
